rv.q: Musical-comedy queens will gag for The Big Gay Jamboree, a cheeky send-up of the form.
The sheer force of Mindelle’s commitment to the bit, so to speak, redeems all.
But whereas “Titaníque” had the casual flair of a tossed-off joke that somehow landed, “The Big Gay Jamboree” works itself into a tizzy with little to show for it.
A laugh-out-loud satire of the American musical wrapped in a surprisingly clever plot about life choices and change, it’s a sparkling example of what intrepid theatermakers can achieve off-Broadway.
Insanity is alive and well and taking up residence at the Orpheum Theatre.
A nonstop cartoon of sexual and social satire, showbiz parodies and wayward silliness, The Big Gay Jamboree swiftly rolls along...
This is one show you won't want to escape.

Stuffed to the brim with pop culture references, musical theatre allusions, and absolute, bat-shit heart, The Big Gay Jamboree is a sturdy, smart musical that, despite some meandering, solidifies Marla Mindelle’s star.
Their entertainment is cattily hilarious, proudly raunchy, and equipped with about three times as much energy as it needs.
Its low brow vibe tends to be corny rather than witty but some theatergoers will find it to their taste.
If you love to laugh, this is one cult you should join.
..has all the earmarks and earworms of another Off Broadway hit.
This potty-mouthed musical does find its fabulously freaky formula inside the ridiculously funny overtures of parody and the love of musical theatre.
This show, like “Titanique” has certainly found its target audience, and will become a cult favorite securing a long run at the Orpheum Theatre.

cn.t: Critics embrace this raunchy, campy send-up of Golden Age musicals, praising its hilarious parody and tuneful pastiche score. While some find it hyperactive and derivative of "Schmigadoon!," most celebrate Mindelle's deranged comedic energy.

vr.q: I thought Big Gay Jamboree was freaking hilarious.
I would still recommend it if you think it's up your alley
